body:
> In Blink, a recent change [issue 41496122](https://issues.chromium.org/issues/41496122) ensured that clicking a label always dispatches a DOMActivate, which might trigger additional activation behavior.

@josepharhar can you comment on why this was changed? Is the behavior in https://wpt.fyi/results/html/semantics/popovers/label-in-invoker.html desired?

I changed the behavior in order to match gecko and webkit, at least for the use case that was presented in that chrome bug: https://issues.chromium.org/issues/41496122#comment9

I'm happy to change the behavior again if gecko and webkit are supportive, and if it doesn't end up breaking websites.

Per [UIEvents DOMActivate](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-DOMActivate), implementers should dispatch `DOMActivate` whenever a label is clicked. So the behavior from the [chromium issue](https://issues.chromium.org/issues/41496122) seems fine. WebKit does the same, and Gecko could consider doing this too.

I looked at the default handler implementation between label and button in Blink and WebKit. When clicking the element:
- A label will default handle the click ([Chromium](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/html/forms/html_label_element.cc;l=170-249;drc=f7cbcc22f6e0a5e10a9f8e6924ca3dc7940ee597), [WebKit](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/410ffc97c838a4713c4b559847c6862252588cad/Source/WebCore/html/HTMLLabelElement.cpp#L157)) and then dispatch `DOMActivate` afterwards. Other elements can still activate off of that `DOMActivate` event.
- A button will dispatch `DOMActivate` on click, default handle the `DOMActivate` ([Chromium](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/html/forms/html_button_element.cc;l=289-374;drc=cf7d8a70bd8d3f9caab2a9e7a306210400ccb9bd), [WebKit](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/c4b2a97359f860ccb76c98122dc77c485076451a/Source/WebCore/html/HTMLButtonElement.cpp#L258)), and then propagate being default handled from `DOMActivate` to the click event ([Chromium](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/dom/node.cc;l=3273-3279;drc=cf7d8a70bd8d3f9caab2a9e7a306210400ccb9bd), [WebKit](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/4586adb9d43392d3c9f158c143e34bad1345da0a/Source/WebCore/dom/Node.cpp#L2692)).

See [test](https://software.hixie.ch/utilities/js/live-dom-viewer/?saved=13765). This has implications on cancelability and timing of events.

Maybe label could also dispatch `DOMActivate` on click and then default handle the `DOMActivate`? For above example, that would mean that if there is a checkbox, only it will activate. And otherwise, the popover will.

From a spec perspective, I don't think this is blocking https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10032 anymore and just points to `DOMActivate` not being precisely defined.
